content.title: Justin Bieber Facing Backlash Over Coachella Performance Amid $10 Million Fee
content.text: Key PointsJustin Bieber headlined Coachella for a record-breaking $10 million over two weekends.Fans criticized his performance as "lazy," mainly featuring YouTube videos and crowd interaction.Despite criticism, he drew massive crowds and featured guest appearances from Dijon and Tems. Late last year news broke that Justin Bieber would be headlining Coachella and that the star singer made a “groundbreaking” amount of money: $10 million for two weekends. “It’s a groundbreaking move for a headliner, and it’s something he built entirely on his own,” a source close to Bieber told Rolling Stone at the time. “Between headlining Coachella and the success of Swag, it’s clear this is the start of an exciting new era for Justin — one where he’s fully in the driver’s seat.” Justin Bieber Called Out Over ‘Lazy’ Coachella Performance The 32-year-old opened Saturday night’s gig sitting in front of a laptop pulling up random YouTube music videos from his past. It was an apparent tribute to the platform on which he was discovered and sang hits such as Baby and Never say Never. Bieber played a number of videos from his adolescence when he was first discovered on the platform and interacted with live comments for the audience, asking how far they wanted to go back with him. The reaction to Bieber’s was mixed, but the overwhelming theme from fans suggested his performance was lazy at best. “The difference in performance quality is actually insane. You’re telling me Justin Bieber is the highest-paid artist at Coachella, and this is what he delivers?” one fan questioned. “Not Justin Bieber scammed Coachella out of $10 million to play songs off of YouTube…” one person wrote. “justin giving the most boring coachella headlining performance men are lazy asf,” offered a third. Justin Bieber Drew Huge Crowd, Set List Included Appearances From Dijon and Tems Bieber drove a raucous crowd to the music festival, leading to a warning for fans from two Los Angeles Times reporters attempting to get to the concert. “Two Times reporters, yours truly included, have been stuck in a sea of Belieber pilgrims for three and a half hours and counting for what would normally be a 15 minute drive to the festival,” the reporters said. “We’re still nowhere near the parking lot, and they’re re-routing fans away from the main entrance if you’re not in the single turn lane. I haven’t seen a crush of traffic like this since Beyoncé headlined.” Bieber’s performance wasn’t just him standing in front of a laptop screen, though, as he welcomed guest performances from Dijon and Tems, among others. Here is his full set list: “All I Can Take” “Speed Demon” “First Place” “Go Baby” “Butterflies” “Walking Away” “All The Way” “405” “Too Long” “Petting Zoo” “I Do” “Stay” with special guest the Kid Laroi “Things You Do” “Glory Voice Memo” “Zuma House” “Dotted Line” “Everything Hallelujah” “Baby” “Favorite Girl” “That Should Be Me” “Beauty and a Beat” “Never Say Never” “Confident” “All That Matters” “With You” (Chris Brown cover) “So Sick” (Ne-Yo cover) “Sorry” “Where Are U Now” “I’m The One” “Yukon” “Devotion” with special guest Dijon “I Think You’re Special” with special guest Tems “Essence” with special guests Tems and Wizkid “Daisies” with special guest Mk.gee Men's Journal NewslettersWe'll keep you in the know on the hottest new gear, whiskey releases, TV shows and movies, and deals everyone's talking about.or sign in withBy signing up I agree to the Terms of Use and acknowledge that I have read the Privacy Policy. Coachella was Bieber’s biggest live show since cancelling the rest of his Justice world tour following health issues in 2022 when the singer revealed he was suffering from issues related to being diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome – a complication from contracting shingles – in 2022. He previously dropped a surprise album, Swag, in July of last year and performed live at the Grammy’s.
